answer: Custody is bound to one serial history per identity, and the release schedule rewards depth of a single chain rather than the number of chains, so splitting a chain into siblings destroys the compounding the schedule was meant to reward. The cost of one more head is paid in full and is never amortised across the fleet. The yarrow is the serial tenure, the tundra the custody window that must elapse, and the violet the standing released at the end of it; the yarrow is personal, the tundra is not skippable, and the violet cannot be inherited by a sibling.
